framework: Cambridge International AS & A Level Travel and Tourism (9395) syllabus 2024–2026
subject: Travel and Tourism

source.publisher: Cambridge University Press & Assessment (Cambridge International Education)

outcomes.text: Describe leisure reasons for travel: relaxation, nature and adventure, sport, health and wellbeing, culture, sightseeing and special interests.
Describe business travel and MICE: meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions.
Explain visiting friends and relatives (VFR) travel.
Describe other reasons for travel, such as medical treatment and religious pilgrimage.
Distinguish domestic, inbound and outbound tourism.
Distinguish mass, packaged, unpackaged and specialist tourism.
Distinguish short-haul from long-haul travel and describe independent travel.
Distinguish sustainable tourism, ecotourism and responsible tourism.

topics.title: 1.3 The changing structure of the travel and tourism industry

outcomes.text: Describe the components: accommodation and catering, travel agents and tour operators, transport providers, visitor attractions and ancillary services.
Explain vertical and horizontal integration.
Explain the rise of independent travel and dynamic packaging.
Explain increasing sustainability awareness and online booking.
Describe resort towns, including beach, seaside and spa resorts, and city destinations.
Describe countryside areas, coastal and island destinations.
Describe purpose-built resorts such as theme parks and all-inclusive resorts.

topics.title: 2.2 The changing appeal of destinations to different external customer types

outcomes.text: Explain accessibility, built and natural attractions, and sustainable practices as parts of destination appeal.
Explain weather and climate, historical and cultural attractions, events and leisure activities.
Explain MICE facilities, accommodation and catering as parts of appeal.
Explain how appeal differs for families, individuals and different age groups, and for groups including educational groups.
Explain how appeal differs for visitors with language and cultural differences and people with specific needs, such as mobility, sensory or dietary needs.

topics.title: 2.3 Changes in travel choices, including by more sustainable means

outcomes.text: Describe changes in travel to destinations by air.
Describe changes in travel on water: cruise ships and ferries.
Describe changes in overland travel, including rail, road, bridges and tunnels.
Describe road options around destinations: cycling, shared transport, buses, coaches, taxis, private hire and cycle or e-scooter hire.
Describe mass and rapid transit rail and water-based transport around destinations.
Describe changing global tourism generating and receiving areas, by place and number of tourists.
Explain how disposable income, employment, national economic strength and exchange rates affect tourism flows.
Explain how government investment and infrastructure developments affect flows.
Explain how age profiles, family structures and attitudes, including sustainability awareness, affect flows.
Explain how epidemics, pollution, disasters, unrest, crime, terrorism and border controls affect flows.
Explain how new transport technology affects flows.
Explain how ICT affects flows: online information, real-time reservations, mobile technology, social media and biometrics.
Explain environmental, social and economic sustainability, ecotourism and responsible tourism.
Explain how environmental, social and economic impacts of tourism drive sustainable tourism.
Explain changing values among customers, providers and governments.
Explain the availability and promotion of sustainable products and increased access to remote areas.
Explain the effect of independent travel, dynamic packaging, education and training programmes, and media influence.
Describe ecotourism products: eco-tours, packages, eco-friendly accommodation and activities.
Describe responsible and ethical behaviour, including respect for environment and culture and following codes of conduct.
Explain how facilities reduce consumption and waste, reuse resources and recycle.
Assess environmental, social and economic impacts of sustainable tourism developments.
Compare attitudes to sustainable tourism among local people and authorities, providers and tourists.

topics.title: 4.1 How travel and tourism organisations serve customers and meet their needs

outcomes.text: Identify types of external customers: families, individuals, groups, visitors with language or cultural differences, and people with specific needs.
Explain external customer needs: suitable products and services, information, assistance, and problem and complaint resolution.
Identify internal customers: staff, suppliers and staff of partner organisations.
Explain internal customer needs: safe workplace, training, knowledge of procedures and standards, and motivation.

topics.title: 4.2 The importance of quality customer service

outcomes.text: Explain benefits to organisations: efficient workforce, satisfaction, loyalty, repeat business, turnover and reputation.
Explain benefits to external customers: positive experience, satisfaction and value for money.
Explain benefits to internal customers: job satisfaction, development and effective teamwork.

topics.title: 4.3 Ways of assessing customer service quality

outcomes.text: Explain setting standards, including benchmarking.
Explain performance management and appraisal.
Explain customer feedback from face-to-face contact, online comments and ratings.
Explain market research techniques: surveys, mystery shoppers, focus groups and observed interactions.

units.title: Paper 2: Planning and Managing a Travel and Tourism Event

outcomes.text: Explain teamwork, team structures and roles such as chairperson, marketing, finance, health and safety, catering and minute taker.
Describe qualities of effective teams and leadership roles such as Belbin.
Explain how to form and call a meeting, agendas and minute taking.
Explain safe use of social media platforms.
Carry out feasibility studies and know the areas to consider.
Use investigative methods such as questionnaires and focus groups.
Carry out a SWOT analysis and a risk assessment.
Use financial methods and estimate costs.
Obtain centre approval and meet legal requirements such as rotas and hiring equipment.
Observe data protection.

topics.title: 5.3 Producing a business plan for your travel and tourism event

outcomes.text: Write a business plan with contingency planning.
Plan timescales and set SMART goals.
Choose methods of monitoring and evaluating the event.
Choose communication methods and prepare financial accounts and payment collection.
Plan safety, data protection and online security.
Plan forms of marketing and design an itinerary.
Keep time and provide customer care and feedback.
Solve problems as they arise.
Gather evidence the event took place, such as witness statements, photographs, screenshots and group chats.
Use techniques to evaluate the event, such as customer feedback by questionnaire, survey and witness statements.
Evaluate the team and reflect on personal performance.
Suggest ways of improving planning, preparing and running the event.

topics.title: 6.1 Defining the tourism market – market research and analysis

outcomes.text: Explain what market research identifies: the market, needs and wants, trends, preferences, popularity and competition.
Place a destination on the Butler Destination Life Cycle model.
Compare primary, secondary, qualitative and quantitative research for advantages, disadvantages and reliability.
Analyse travel trends and preferences statistically.
Carry out a SWOT analysis and a PESTLE analysis.
Segment the market by travel motivation, demographics, psychographics and geography.
Build visitor profiles: length of stay, accommodation, spending power, activities, media and booking method.
Explain product positioning: image and reputation, differentiation and the unique selling point.
Review the marketing mix: product, price, place and promotion.
Explain reasons for branding a destination.
Describe characteristics of an effective destination brand.
Create a brand identity: name, slogan, logo, USP, colour, price, packaging and corporate identity.
Plan a brand launch: timing, costs, guardians, objectives, communication, materials and campaign.
Explain roles of interdependent stakeholders: NTOs, regional and local organisations, commercial and non-commercial organisations and the community.
List methods of raising awareness: websites, publicity, social media, email, public relations, advertising, sales promotion, word of mouth and signage.
Choose methods by cost, reach, 24-hour marketing, lead times, personalisation and trackability.
Distinguish owned, paid, earned and shared media.
Explain challenges from varied products, intangibility, negative reputation, many partners, limited funding, a competitive market and disasters or unrest.

topics.title: 6.5 Monitoring the effectiveness of the destination brand

outcomes.text: Describe methods of monitoring a brand: resources invested, marketing activities, surveys, web traffic, SEO, social media response and trade fair attendance.
Use KPIs: popularity ranking, arrivals, visitor spend, length of stay, occupancy, jobs, market share and brand awareness.

topics.title: 7.1 Organisations involved in destination management, their roles and priorities

outcomes.text: Explain roles of governments, ministries and NTOs: strategy, research, funding and priorities.
Explain roles of local authorities and regional organisations: land use, planning control, infrastructure, promotion and visitor management.
Explain the role of NGOs in research, funding, expertise, training and raising awareness.
Explain commercial organisations: overseas travel agents and tour operators, and local businesses.
Explain Destination Management Companies and their ground services.
Describe sustainable policies, new products, visitor and traffic management, and branding and marketing.
Describe partnerships, long-term investment, community involvement, planning control and widening access.
Describe environmental auditing, visitor communication, monitoring and encouraging responsible tourist behaviour.
Explain economic objectives such as retaining visitor spending and funding community projects.
Explain environmental objectives such as limiting harm, conservation and sustainable resource use.
Explain sociocultural objectives such as protecting culture, community empowerment, access, jobs and education.
Explain political objectives such as image, reputation and international relations.
Explain positive economic impacts: income, foreign exchange, jobs, development, infrastructure and the multiplier effect.
Explain negative economic impacts: leakages, low pay, over-dependency, seasonality, lost traditional jobs and higher costs and taxes.
Explain positive environmental impacts: improved assets, conservation, regeneration, regulations and sustainable practices.
Explain negative environmental impacts: resource pressure, congestion, erosion, land degradation, pollution and wildlife disruption.
Explain positive sociocultural impacts: preserving customs and crafts, facilities, cultural understanding and community empowerment.
Explain negative sociocultural impacts: host conflict, family change, social problems, lost identity, demonstration effect, commodification and heritage damage.
